messages:
alex: Morning async — quick SRE check-in.

What I did: rolled the kv-eviction tuning (canary) to 3 hosts, verified no spike in 95th latency.
Blockers: still seeing ~2% of requests hit fallback model variant in us-west-2 during bursts, not sure why.
Today: follow up on fallback routing rule, PR review for alert debounce change.

maria: Nice. Can you paste the canary job id?

alex: job/kv-evict-canary-3312

lee: On fallback routing — I noticed the policy selector doesn't match the new label 'tier:dedicated' for some hostgroups. Quick grep showed missing tag in the autoscaler config.

kai: I'll add a hotfix to autoscaler config and run a dry-run. @alex can you re-run the failing burst test after I push?

alex: Yep will re-run in ~30m. Also pinging @maria for the alert debounce PR review — it's small.

maria: Looking now. Two comments inline about the timeout value.

oncall-bot: ping — active oncall: kai (shift ends in 4h). Reminder: escalate to oncall@redwood if SLO error > 5% sustained.

lee: For the 2% fallback — I can patch routing to prefer cache-warmed hosts first. If that fails, we fallback to model-quantized-1.

alex: That plan sounds good. If warm-first doesn't reduce fallback rate, we'll revert the kv-evict change.

maria: Reviewed PR LGTM after adjusting timeout to 1.2s.

kai: Hotfix pushed to autoscaler config: added 'tier:dedicated' selector. Dry-run shows expected host assignment. @alex, ready for your burst.

alex: Running burst test now. Will post results.

alex: Test done — fallback rate down to 0.3%, 95p latency unchanged. Marking canary healthy and promoting to remaining hosts.

maria: Thanks — will merge debounce PR and cut a small release.

lee: I'll schedule a short doc update for routing rules and add the hotfix note.

alex: Done for today. No further blockers. :thumbsup:
